info.title: DTN Renewables API
info.description:
# Introduction
Welcome to DTN’s Renewables API.  This service empowers consumers with accurate, global, location-specific environmental data tailored for the renewable energy industry.  It caters to a wide range of scenarios, including:
  * Developers optimizing site selection, turbine placement, and operational strategies for wind energy projects.
  * Analysts simulating renewable energy generation, forecasting power output, and assessing project viability.
  * Grid operators anticipating fluctuations in renewable energy supply that affect stability and efficiency.
  * Institutions involved in research and development to enhance renewable energy technologies.
  * Consultants assessing environmental impacts for compliance with regulatory requirements.


Key Features:


  * Obtain a detailed time series of environmental data for any location on Earth at hourly or sub-hourly intervals up to 15 days ahead, backed by DTN’s innovative global models and state-of-the-art cloud technology.
  * Access essential content such as hub height wind speed, gust, and direction anywhere from 10 to 300 meters above ground level.
  * Aggregate data on-the-fly over multiple hours using easy-to-understand query arguments.
  * Specify a time range with UTC offsets to automatically convert the response to any local time zone for faster interpretation and integration into local operations.


The interactive documentation that follows is a guide to setting up requests, understanding responses, and leveraging all the features of the Renewables API.
# Getting Started
## Obtaining credentials
To get started, all users need their own client ID and client secret. Please contact an account manager or the [DTN sales team](https://www.dtn.com/contact-us/) to obtain these. Then, review the `Authentication` section to learn how to request an API access token. Do not share or use others' API credentials, since doing so may compromise information security.

## Making requests
There are multiple ways to make an initial API request:

**1. Interactive documentation:** Navigate to the `Authentication` section on this page, insert credentials to obtain an access token, then explore the API endpoints described in the `Endpoints` section.

**2. Postman collection:** For a hands-on approach, consider downloading the Postman collection and environment from the top of this page. Insert credentials and start testing the API in Postman's interactive application.

**3. Writing code:** Ready to start coding? Try the Python example below, replacing `client_id` and `client_secret` with proper credentials.  This invokes the forecast endpoint for hub height winds with a GET request and prints the response.

```python
  import requests
  import urllib

  #--- Obtain an API access token ---

  auth_url = 'https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize'

  body = {
      'grant_type': 'client_credentials',
      'client_id': '...insert your client id here...',
      'client_secret': '...insert your client secret here...',
      'audience': 'https://renewables.api.dtn.com'
  }
  response = requests.post(auth_url, json=body)
  access_token = response.json()['data']['access_token']

  #--- Invoke the API ---

  api_base_url = 'https://renewables.api.dtn.com/v1'
  query_parameters = urllib.parse.urlencode({
      "lat": 35.47,
      "lon": -97.51,
      "startTime": "2024-10-01T00:06:10Z",
      "endTime": "2024-10-14T00:06:10Z",
  })
  endpoint = '/hub-height-winds/forecast?' + query_parameters

  headers = {'Authorization': 'Bearer ' + access_token}
  response = requests.get(api_base_url + endpoint, headers=headers)

  #--- Print the response ---

  print(response.json())
```

tags.name: Parameters
tags.description:
Renewables API currently offers environmental parameters for a forecast time range up to 15 days in the future.

It’s possible to aggregate most parameters over multiple hours.  The tables that follow identify which parameters have corresponding aggregation parameter names.  To request an aggregation, just substitute the desired parameter name and specify an `interval` greater than 1 hour (see `Endpoints` section for details).  For example, if 100-meter wind speed (`windSpeed100m`) has corresponding parameters `windSpeed100mMax`, `windSpeed100mMin`, and `windSpeed100mAvg`, request parameter `windSpeed100mAvg` with `interval=6h` in the query string to obtain the 6-hour 100-meter wind speed average.
## Hub Height Winds Parameters
Expand the table below to view parameters available from the hub height winds endpoint and each one's description, unit of measurement, and whether it is a default. The API returns only defaults unless specific parameters are requested.
<details> <summary>Click to expand...</summary>

| Parameter               | Default | Description | Metric units | Imperial units | Aggregation Parameters |
|-------------------------|---------|-------------|--------------|----------------|------------------------|
| localOffsetHours        |         | The number of hours to add or subtract from the UTC timestamp in the response to obtain local time (accounting for Daylight Saving Time) at the requested latitude and longitude. | number of hours | number of hours | |
| localTimezoneOlson      |         | The Olson time zone name at the requested latitude and longitude. | name of the timezone | name of the timezone | |
| windDirection100m       | Yes     | The direction from which the wind is blowing at a height of 100 meters above the ground, measured in degrees with respect to true north. | degree | degree | windDirection100mAvg |
| windDirection{n}m       |         | The direction from which the wind is blowing at a height of {n} meters above the ground (any whole number from 10-300), measured in degrees with respect to true north. | degree | degree | windDirection{n}mAvg |
| windGust100m            | Yes     | The wind gust speed at a height of 100 meters above the ground. | meter per second | mile per hour | windGust100mMax, windGust100mMin, windGust100mAvg |
| windGust{n}m            |         | The wind gust speed at a height of {n} meters above the ground (any whole number from 10-300). | meter per second | mile per hour | windGust{n}mMax, windGust{n}mMin, windGust{n}mAvg |
| windSpeed100m           | Yes     | The wind speed at a height of 100 meters above the ground. | meter per second | mile per hour | windSpeed100mMax, windSpeed100mMin, windSpeed100mAvg |
| windSpeed{n}m           |         | The wind speed at a height of {n} meters above the ground (any whole number from 10-300). | meter per second | mile per hour | windSpeed{n}mMax, windSpeed{n}mMin, windSpeed{n}mAvg |
| windSpeed10mLowerBound  |         | Lower bound on the uncertainty in the 10-meter wind speed.  | meter per second | mile per hour | |
| windSpeed10mUpperBound  |         | Upper bound on the uncertainty in the 10-meter wind speed.  | meter per second | mile per hour | |
| windSpeed100mLowerBound |         | Lower bound on the uncertainty in the 100-meter wind speed. | meter per second | mile per hour | |
| windSpeed100mUpperBound |         | Upper bound on the uncertainty in the 100-meter wind speed. | meter per second | mile per hour | |
</details>

## Solar Irradiance Parameters
Expand the table below to view parameters available from the solar irradiance endpoint and each one's description, unit of measurement, and whether it is a default. The API returns only defaults unless specific parameters are requested.
<details> <summary>Click to expand...</summary>

| Parameter                    | Default | Description | Metric units | Imperial units | Aggregation Parameters |
|------------------------------|---------|-------------|--------------|----------------|------------------------|
| airTemp                      | Yes     | Air temperature at 2 meters above ground level. | degree Celsius | degree Fahrenheit | airTempMax, airTempMin, airTempAvg |
| directNormalIrradiance       | Yes     | Direct Normal Irradiance (DNI) is the portion of instantaneous solar radiation reaching the Earth's surface that is perpendicular to the sun's rays, excluding diffuse sunlight. | watt per square meter | watt per square meter | directNormalIrradianceMax, directNormalIrradianceMin, directNormalIrradianceAvg |
| diffuseHorizontalIrradiance  | Yes     | Diffuse Horizontal Irradiance (DHI) is the portion of instantaneous solar radiation reaching the Earth's surface that has been scattered by the atmosphere, excluding direct sunlight. | watt per square meter | watt per square meter | diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMax, diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMin, diffuseHorizontalIrradianceAvg |
| globalNormalIrradiance       | Yes     | Global Normal Irradiance (GNI) is the total amount of solar radiation reaching the Earth's surface that is perpendicular to the sun's rays, including both direct and diffuse sunlight. | watt per square meter | watt per square meter | globalNormalIrradianceMax, globalNormalIrradianceMin, globalNormalIrradianceAvg |
| globalRadiation              | Yes     | Total mean incoming solar radiation received on the Earth's surface, combining both direct sunlight and diffuse sky radiation over the past hour. | joule per square centimeter | joule per square centimeter | globalRadiationSum |
| localOffsetHours             |         | The number of hours to add or subtract from the UTC timestamp in the response to obtain local time (accounting for Daylight Saving Time) at the requested latitude and longitude. | number of hours | number of hours | |
| localTimezoneOlson           |         | The Olson time zone name at the requested latitude and longitude. | name of the timezone | name of the timezone | |
| snowfallAmount               | Yes     | Total accumulation of snow (measured as depth, not liquid equivalent). | millimeter | inch | snowfallAmountSum |
| shortWaveRadiation           | Yes     | Also called Global Horizontal Irradiance (GHI), this is the instantaneous high-energy solar radiation received at the Earth's surface, including both direct (DNI) and diffuse (DHI) sunlight. | watt per square meter | watt per square meter | shortWaveRadiationMax, shortWaveRadiationMin, shortWaveRadiationAvg |
</details>

get.description:
This endpoint provides forecast wind parameters from 10-300 meters above ground level for any point on Earth. Specify the location, parameters of interest, and a time range from now until 15 days ahead. The API responds with the requested time series in GeoJSON format.

Use the query string to customize the results in the response body:

  * Specify a location as latitude (`lat`) and longitude (`lon`).  These are required.

  * Specify `parameters` to filter the response to a specific, comma-separated list of environmental parameters. The API returns defaults when this is omitted.

  * Specify `startTime` and `endTime` (using [RFC 3339](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc3339#section-5.8) format) for a forecast time range, or `startTime` alone for just one timestamp.

  * Specify `units=us-std` to receive values as United States customary (imperial) units. The API returns metric units by default and when `units=si-std` is expressly requested.

  * Specify `interval` to obtain sub-hourly (interpolated) or multi-hour (aggregated) results. The API returns hourly results by default.

All together, a complete request looks like:

```
https://renewables.api.dtn.com/v1/hub-height-winds/forecast?lat={lat}&lon={lon}&startTime={start_time}&endTime={end_time}&interval={interval}&parameters={param1,param2}&units={units}
```

### How to change timesteps

To interpolate to sub-hourly timesteps, specify `interval=15m`, `interval=30m`, or `interval=45m` in the query string.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=15m&parameters=windDirection10m,windSpeed10m`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=30m&parameters=windDirection10m,windSpeed10m`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=45m&parameters=windDirection10m,windSpeed10m`

To aggregate over multiple hours, specify `interval={n}h` in the query string using a whole number of hours for `{n}`, from 2 to the timespan between `startTime` and `endTime`. Also, substitute the desired aggregation parameter names from the `Parameters` section. For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=2h&parameters=windDirection10mAvg,windSpeed10mMax`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=6h&parameters=windDirection10mAvg,windSpeed10mMax`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=24h&parameters=windDirection10mAvg,windSpeed10mMax`

In special cases, daily aggregations might require local timezone-aware aggregations to account of days with an one extra or less hour.  In these cases, specify `interval=1d` along with timezone-aware `startTime` and `endTime` values.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-11-03T00:00:00&endTime=2024-11-04T23:59:59&interval=1d&parameters=windDirection10mAvg,windSpeed10mMax`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-03-09T00:00:00&endTime=2024-03-10T23:59:59&interval=1d&parameters=windDirection10mAvg,windSpeed10mMax`

### How to change timezones

Typically, `startTime` and `endTime` end with `Z` to indicate UTC time.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z`

To change timezones, specify a UTC offset (such as `+08:00` or `-05:00`) instead of `Z`. Note that the `+` symbol is a special URL character that must be encoded as `%2B`.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00-05:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00-05:00`
  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00%2B08:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00%2B08:00`
  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00-05:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00%2B08:00`

To obtain the local timezone at the requested location, omit the suffix entirely. For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00`
  * Fractional time zones
      + Parameters:
        + **startTime:** 2025-07-04T00:00:00
        + **endTime:** 2025-07-04T23:59:59
        + **interval:** 24h
        + **lat:** 30.251
        + **lon:** 62.569
        
      + Response:
        ```json
        "properties": {
            "2025-07-03T23:30:00+0430": {
                "windDirection100mAvg": 309,
                "windGust100mMax": 8.6,
                "windGust100mMin": 4.9,
                "windGust100mAvg": 6.2,
                "windSpeed100mMax": 6.6,
                "windSpeed100mMin": 3.2,
                "windSpeed100mAvg": 4.3
            },
            "2025-07-04T23:30:00+0430": {
                "windDirection100mAvg": 325,
                "windGust100mMax": 8.1,
                "windGust100mMin": 8.1,
                "windGust100mAvg": 8.1,
                "windSpeed100mMax": 6,
                "windSpeed100mMin": 6,
                "windSpeed100mAvg": 6
            }
        }
        ```
      * Explanation:
        * **Why** This response seems confusing at first becuase we have 2 data points when we seemingly only requested a single 24 hour interval.
        * **Local Timezone Assumption** When requesting a start and end time that has no timezone, the timezone of the location requested will be used.
          * For the example requested lat/lon the local timezone is UTC+04:30 (fractional timezone)
        * **Inclusive Time Range** startTime is hour inclusive, meaning the API will return data for the top of the requested hour (in UTC).
        * **UTC Conversion** All data is stored in UTC hourly.
          * When we convert these requested timestamps to UTC, `startTime=2025-07-03T19:30:00Z`, `endTime=2025-07-04T19:29:59Z`
        * Since startTime and endTime are `inclusive`, so the time range spans exactly 25 hours, not 24.
        * Changing `endTime` to `2025-07-04T23:00:00` will result in a single interval returned.

In all cases, timestamps in the API response automatically match the timezone indicated by `startTime`.

package main

import (
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"io/ioutil"
)

func main() {

	url := "https://renewables.api.dtn.com/v1/hub-height-winds/forecast?lat=SOME_NUMBER_VALUE&lon=SOME_NUMBER_VALUE&startTime=SOME_STRING_VALUE&endTime=SOME_STRING_VALUE&interval=SOME_STRING_VALUE&parameters=SOME_ARRAY_VALUE&units=SOME_STRING_VALUE"

	req, _ := http.NewRequest("GET", url, nil)

	req.Header.Add("Accept-Encoding", "SOME_STRING_VALUE")
	req.Header.Add("Accept", "SOME_STRING_VALUE")
	req.Header.Add("Authorization", "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN")

	res, _ := http.DefaultClient.Do(req)

	defer res.Body.Close()
	body, _ := ioutil.ReadAll(res.Body)

	fmt.Println(res)
	fmt.Println(string(body))

}

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=30m&parameters=directNormalIrradiance,diffuseHorizontalIrradiance`

To aggregate over multiple hours, specify `interval={n}h` in the query string using a whole number of hours for `{n}`, from 2 to the timespan between `startTime` and `endTime`. Also, substitute the desired aggregation parameter names from the `Parameters` section. For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=2h&parameters=directNormalIrradianceAvg,diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMax`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=6h&parameters=directNormalIrradianceAvg,diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMax`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z&interval=24h&parameters=directNormalIrradianceAvg,diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMax`

In some cases, daily aggregations might require local timezone-aware aggregations to account of days with an one extra or less hour.  In these cases, specify `interval=1d` along with timezone-aware `startTime` and `endTime` values.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-11-03T00:00:00&endTime=2024-11-04T23:59:59&interval=1d&parameters=directNormalIrradianceAvg,diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMax`

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-03-09T00:00:00&endTime=2024-03-10T23:59:59&interval=1d&parameters=directNormalIrradianceAvg,diffuseHorizontalIrradianceMax`

### How to change timezones

Typically, `startTime` and `endTime` end with `Z` to indicate UTC time.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00Z&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00Z`

To change timezones, specify a UTC offset (such as `+08:00` or `-05:00`) instead of `Z`. Note that the `+` symbol is a special URL character that must be encoded as `%2B`.  For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00-05:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00-05:00`
  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00%2B08:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00%2B08:00`
  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00-05:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00%2B08:00`

To obtain the local timezone at the requested location, omit the suffix entirely. For example:

  * `?lat=35.47&lon=-97.51&startTime=2024-10-01T00:00:00&endTime=2024-10-10T00:00:00`
  * Fractional time zones
      + Parameters:
        + **startTime:** 2025-07-04T00:00:00
        + **endTime:** 2025-07-04T23:59:59
        + **interval:** 24h
        + **lat:** 30.251
        + **lon:** 62.569
        
      + Response:
        ```json
          "properties": {
          "2025-07-03T23:30:00+0430": {
              "airTempMax": 40.1,
          },
          "2025-07-04T23:30:00+0430": {
              "airTempMax": 30.2,
          }
        }
        ```
      * Explanation:
        * **Why** This response seems confusing at first becuase we have 2 data points when we seemingly only requested a single 24 hour interval.
        * **Local Timezone Assumption** When requesting a start and end time that has no timezone, the timezone of the location requested will be used.
          * For the example requested lat/lon the local timezone is UTC+04:30 (fractional timezone)
        * **Inclusive Time Range** startTime is hour inclusive, meaning the API will return data for the top of the requested hour (in UTC).
        * **UTC Conversion** All data is stored in UTC hourly.
          * When we convert these requested timestamps to UTC, `startTime=2025-07-03T19:30:00Z`, `endTime=2025-07-04T19:29:59Z`
        * Since startTime and endTime are `inclusive`, so the time range spans exactly 25 hours, not 24.
        * Changing `endTime` to `2025-07-04T23:00:00` will result in a single interval returned.

In all cases, timestamps in the API response automatically match the timezone indicated by `startTime`.

clientCredentials.description:
# Using DAIS for M2M/API Auth
You have been given a Client ID and a Client Secret, which are used to request a DTN Access Token. DTN Access Tokens are required when making calls to each and every DTN API endpoint. The following information provides additional details on these tokens and how they are generated.
## What is an Access Token and how is it different from an API Key?
An API Key is a random string of characters that an API uses to authorize whether or not a calling client has approved access to an endpoint. These keys are a non-standard approach to API authorization and are generally issued on a per-API basis.

An Access Token is also a string of characters but is a base-64 encoded JavaScript Object Notation Web Token, or JWT. JWTs are a widely accepted standard that use OAuth concepts and approaches. 

Both API Keys and Access Tokens are used in an Authorization Request Header as a Bearer, meaning there is no difference in where you put this string of characters when you make calls to DTN APIs.
## How to generate an Access Token?
When requested, an Access Token is generated for your specific Client (ID/Secret) and for a specific API. The DTN Auth and Identity Service (DAIS) generates new Access Tokens for your client. The DAIS endpoint is `POST https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize`.

This endpoint takes two Header parameters:
  * `Content-Type: application/json`
  * `Accept: application/json`

This endpoint takes four parameters in the Request Body:
  * `grant_type`: this should always be client_credentials for generating machine-to-machine tokens.
  * `client_id`: this is the Client ID or Application ID using the token and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This ID will never change for your client/application.
  * `client_secret`: this is the Client Secret that is associated with the Application ID and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This key is subject to rotation for security purposes but always with the client's knowledge.
  * `audience`: this is the API for which this Access Token will be used. For the DTN Renewables API, you need to use the following audience: https://renewables.api.dtn.com

You can use this CURL command template as a reference for obtaining an access token:
  ```
  curl --location --request POST 'https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
"grant_type": "client_credentials",
"client_id": "insert your client id here",
"client_secret": "insert your client secret here",
"audience": "insert your audience here"
}' 
  ```

*This document, for demonstration purposes, supplies a client_id and client_secret in all code examples. This client/application is for a fictitious API and cannot be used in practice to gain unauthorized access to any other DTN API.*
Upon generating a new Access Token, you should receive an HTTP Response from DAIS similar to this:
  ```
  {
    "data": {
          "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw",
          "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
          "expires_in": 90,
          "token_type": "Bearer"
      },
      "meta": {
          "date_time": "2022-06-24T19:09:42.963Z",
          "name": "v1.tokens.authorize",
          "uuid": "ee6f9feb-dcf8-4421-a6fd-efd6beabdaa9",
          "start_timestamp": 1656097782509,
          "end_timestamp": 1656097782963,
          "execution_time": 454
      }
  }
  ```
Looking at this Response, you will see:
  * `access_token`: contains the JWT Access Token string you will use as your Bearer token.
  * `scope`: contains the scopes that this Access Token gives you permissions to access.
  * `expires_in`: contains the length of time before this Access Token will expire, in seconds.
  * `token_type`: verifies that this Access Token should be used as a Bearer token.

## How to use an Access Token after one is generated?
Once a new Access Token is obtained, it is used in each call to a DTN API endpoint as a Bearer token in an Authorization Request Header. For example:

## Deconstructing the Access Token
A DTN Access Token carries information within its JWT Body that is available on every API call. By deconstructing the JWT token, our Access Tokens will resemble:
  ```
  {
    "https://auth.dtn.com/customerId": "1234567890Demo",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/productCode": "DemoApiP",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp": "18.213.174.27",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/rps": "100",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/tier": "Basic",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/quota": "999999",
    "iss": "https://id.auth.dtn.com/",
    "sub": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM@clients",
    "aud": "https://demo-api.auth.dtn.com/",
    "iat": 1656099068,
    "exp": 1656099158,
    "azp": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM",
    "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
    "gty": "client-credentials",
    "permissions": [
      "read:demo",
      "create:demo",
      "update:demo"
    ]
  }
  ```
### Description of Claims

  | Claim                              | Type                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
  | -----------------------------------| --------------------------------------------| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/customerId`  | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Customer ID found in the DTN Order Management/Salesforce system associated with this token.                                                                                                |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/productCode` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Identity product code associated with this token.                                                                                                                                          |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the IP address of the requesting client.                                                                                                                                                       |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/rps`         | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum rate per second this customer is authorized to utilize.                                                                                                                            |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/tier`        | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the data tier the customer purchased for the requested access.                                                                                                                                 |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/quota`       | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum yearly quota the customer purchased for calling DTN endpoints for the specific product.                                                                                            |
  | `iss`                              | String (URI)                                | The Security Token Service (STS) that issues and returns the token. If this value is not from `https://id.auth.dtn.com/`, the token should not be considered trusted.                                                      |
  | `sub`                              | String (URI)                                | The principle about which the token asserts information (the User ID or Client ID within the Identity Provider). A User ID will start with a prefix of `auth0\|`, while the Client ID will end with the suffix `@clients`. |
  | `aud`                              | String \| Array (Strings) (URI \| [URI, …]) | Identifies the intended recipient(s) of the token – its audience. The token should be rejected if the audience does not contain values expected by the calling application.                                                |
  | `iat`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | “Issued At” indicates when the authentication for this token occurred.                                                                                                                                                     |
  | `exp`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | The “expiration time” on or after which the JWT must not be accepted for processing.                                                                                                                                       |
  | `azp`                              | String                                      | The application/client ID of the client using the token. The application can cat as itself or on behalf of a user.                                                                                                         |
  | `gty`                              | String (Space-delimited)                    | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |
  | `permissions`                      | Array (Strings)                             | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |
